You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

        self.routes=routes

            def do_PUT(self): self.handle_m()
            def handle_m(self):

                outer.reqs.append((self.command, self.path, dict(self.headers), body))
                key=(self.command, self.path)

import subprocess, threading, http.server, socket, sys, os, json, time, urllib.parse

class Server:
    def __init__(self, routes, default=(404, "not found", {})):
        # routes: dict path -> (code, body, headers) or callable(path, headers, method) -> (code, body, headers)
        # keys can also be tuple(method,path)
        self.routes=routes
        self.default=default
        self.reqs=[]
        outer=self
        class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def do_GET(self): self.handle_m()
            def do_HEAD(self): self.handle_m()
            def do_POST(self): self.handle_m()
            def do_PUT(self): self.handle_m()
            def handle_m(self):
                length=int(self.headers.get('Content-Length',0) or 0)
                body=self.rfile.read(length) if length else b''
                outer.reqs.append((self.command, self.path, dict(self.headers), body))
                key=(self.command, self.path)
                val=outer.routes.get(key, outer.routes.get(self.path, outer.default))
                if callable(val):
                    val=val(self.path, dict(self.headers), self.command, body)
                code, content, hdrs = val
                if isinstance(content, str): content=content.encode()
                self.send_response(code)
                for k,v in hdrs.items():
                    self.send_header(k,v)
                if 'Content-Length' not in hdrs and 'content-length' not in [x.lower() for x in hdrs]:
                    self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(content)))
                self.end_headers()
                if self.command!='HEAD':
                    self.wfile.write(content)
            def log_message(self, *a): pass
        self.httpd=http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1",0), H)
        self.port=self.httpd.server_address[1]
        self.thread=threading.Thread(target=self.httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    def __enter__(self):
        self.thread.start(); return self
    def __exit__(self,*a):
        self.httpd.shutdown(); self.httpd.server_close()
    @property
    def base(self): return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}/"
    def paths(self): return [(m,p) for m,p,h,b in self.reqs]

def run_scan(routes, args_extra=[], words=["a","b","dir","file"], default=(404,"not found",{}), exe="./executable", base_path="", timeout=15, env=None):
    with Server(routes, default) as srv:
        base=srv.base+base_path
        wl="/tmp/wl_test.txt"
        with open(wl,"w") as f: f.write("\n".join(words)+"\n" if words else "")
        args=[exe, base, "-w", wl, "--no-color"]+args_extra
        # allow args_extra to override base handling if contains {BASE}
        args=[a.replace("{BASE}",srv.base) for a in args]
        r=subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=env)
        print(f"CMD {args} EXIT {r.returncode}")
        print("STDOUT:"); print(r.stdout, end="" if r.stdout.endswith("\n") or not r.stdout else "\n[nonl]\n")
        print("STDERR:"); print(r.stderr, end="" if not r.stderr or r.stderr.endswith("\n") else "\n[nonl]\n")
        print("REQS:", srv.paths())
        return r, srv.reqs

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from harness import *
# default diff negative side: body=p, validator url_len-size=22

 "/same_sign": lambda p,h,m,b:(200,"x"*(7+len(h.get("Host",""))+len(p)-22),{}),

 "/diff_code": lambda p,h,m,b:(201,"x"*(7+len(h.get("Host",""))+len(p)-22),{}),
}
run_scan(routes,["-t","3","-T","1"],words=list(routes.keys())+ ["missing"],default=lambda p,h,m,b:(200,p,{}))
# default diff positive side: body = p + 50 Xs (size=url_len+28 since p len11 vs url33 =>61 diff28), routes opposite variations
routes2={
 "/same_sign": lambda p,h,m,b:(200,"x"*(7+len(h.get("Host",""))+len(p)+28),{}),
 "/opp_sign": lambda p,h,m,b:(200,"x"*(7+len(h.get("Host",""))+len(p)-28),{}),
}
run_scan(routes2,["-t","3","-T","1"],words=list(routes2.keys())+ ["missing"],default=lambda p,h,m,b:(200,p+("X"*50),{}))

routes3={
 "/exact":(200,"123456789",{}),

}
run_scan(routes3,["-t","3","-T","1"],words=list(routes3.keys()),default=(200,"123456789",{}))

routes4={
 "/same_dest":(301,"xx",{"Location":"/home"}),
 "/diff_dest":(301,"xx",{"Location":"/other"}),

}
run_scan(routes4,["-t","3","-T","1"],words=["same_dest","diff_dest","same_dest_diffcode","no_redir_301_body"],default=(301,"", {"Location":"/home"}))
PY
cat /tmp/v5.txt"}

use clap::builder::PossibleValuesParser;
use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, ArgGroup, Command};
use std::num::NonZeroU32;
use std::path::PathBuf;

fn single(id: &'static str, long: &'static str, value_name: &'static str, help: &'static str) -> Arg {
    Arg::new(id)
        .long(long)
        .value_name(value_name)
        .help(help)
        .action(ArgAction::Set)
}

fn single_short(
    id: &'static str,
    short: char,
    long: &'static str,
    value_name: &'static str,
    help: &'static str,
) -> Arg {
    single(id, long, value_name, help).short(short)
}

fn append_short(
    id: &'static str,
    short: char,
    long: &'static str,
    value_name: &'static str,
    help: &'static str,
) -> Arg {
    Arg::new(id)
        .short(short)
        .long(long)
        .value_name(value_name)
        .help(help)
        .action(ArgAction::Append)
}

fn multi_short(
    id: &'static str,
    short: char,
    long: &'static str,
    value_name: &'static str,
    help: &'static str,
) -> Arg {
    Arg::new(id)
        .short(short)
        .long(long)
        .value_name(value_name)
        .help(help)
        .num_args(1..)
        .value_delimiter(',')
        .action(ArgAction::Append)
}

fn flag(id: &'static str, long: &'static str, help: &'static str) -> Arg {
    Arg::new(id)
        .long(long)
        .help(help)
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
}

fn flag_short(id: &'static str, short: char, long: &'static str, help: &'static str) -> Arg {
    flag(id, long, help).short(short)
}

pub fn command() -> Command {
    Command::new("Dirble")
        .version("1.4.2 (commit c11e5cd, build 2026-08-10)")
        .about("Fast directory scanning and scraping tool")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .next_line_help(true)
        .max_term_width(100)
        .disable_colored_help(true)
        .after_help(
            "OUTPUT FORMAT:\n    + [url] - File\n    D [url] - Directory\n    L [url] - Listable Directory\n\nEXAMPLE USE:\n    - Run against a website using the default dirble_wordlist.txt from the\n      current directory:\n        dirble [address]\n\n    - Run with a different wordlist and including .php and .html extensions:\n        dirble [address] -w example_wordlist.txt -x .php,.html\n\n    - With listable directory scraping enabled:\n        dirble [address] --scrape-listable\n\n    - Providing a list of extensions and a list of URIs:\n        dirble [address] -X wordlists/web.lst -U uri-list.txt\n\n    - Providing multiple hosts to scan via command line:\n        dirble [address] -u [address] -u [address]",
        )
        .group(
            ArgGroup::new("hosts")
                .args(["uri", "uri_file", "uri_opt"])
                .required(true)
                .multiple(true),
        )
        .group(
            ArgGroup::new("extension_group")
                .args(["extensions", "extension_file"])
                .multiple(true),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("uri")
                .value_name("uri")
                .help("The URI of the host to scan, optionally supports basic auth with\nhttp://user:pass@host:port")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(url::Url)),
        )
        .arg(
            append_short("uri_opt", 'u', "uri", "uri", "Additional hosts to scan")
                .visible_alias("url")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(url::Url)),
        )
        .arg(
            append_short(
                "uri_file",
                'U',
                "uri-file",
                "uri-file",
                "The filename of a file containing a list of URIs to scan - cookies and\nheaders set will be applied to all URIs",
            )
            .visible_alias("url-file")
            .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(PathBuf)),
        )

            single("http_verb", "verb", "http_verb", "Specify which HTTP verb to use")

        .arg(
            append_short(

                "wordlist",

fn dispatch_job(
    job: ScanJob,
    opts: &Arc<GlobalOpts>,
    output_tx: &Sender<OutputMessage>,
    scan_tx: &Sender<ScanMessage>,
    active_workers: &mut usize,
    scanned: &mut BTreeSet<Url>,
) {
    scanned.insert(job.folder.clone());
    for prefix in opts.prefixes.iter() {
        for extension in opts.extensions.iter() {
            let transformed: Vec<String> = opts
                .wordlist
                .iter()
                .map(|word| {
                    let extended = if opts.ext_sub {
                        word.replace("%EXT%", extension)
                    } else {
                        format!("{}{}", word, extension)
                    };
                    format!("{}{}", prefix, extended)
                })
                .collect();
            for index in 0..job.split {
                let sublist: Vec<String> = transformed
                    .iter()
                    .skip(index as usize)
                    .step_by(job.split as usize)
                    .cloned()
                    .collect();
                let worker_job = job.clone();
                let worker_opts = Arc::clone(opts);
                let worker_output = output_tx.clone();
                let worker_scan = scan_tx.clone();
                *active_workers += 1;
                thread::spawn(move || {
                    request_thread(worker_job, sublist, worker_opts, worker_output, worker_scan)
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

pub fn scan_manager(
    receiver: Receiver<ScanMessage>,
    scan_tx: Sender<ScanMessage>,
    initial_sender: Sender<Vec<ScanJob>>,
    output_tx: Sender<OutputMessage>,
    opts: Arc<GlobalOpts>,
) {
    let mut client = CurlClient::new();
    let mut scanned: BTreeSet<Url> = BTreeSet::new();

    // Wait for the request to prepare the initial targets.
    while let Ok(message) = receiver.recv() {
        if matches!(message, ScanMessage::Initial) {
            break;
        }
    }

    if opts.max_recursion_depth.map(|depth| depth < 0).unwrap_or(false) {
        loop {
            thread::park();
        }
    }

    let recursion_prevented = opts.disable_recursion || opts.max_recursion_depth == Some(0);
    let has_non_directory_host = opts
        .hosts
        .iter()
        .any(|host| !host.path().ends_with('/'));
    let problematic = recursion_prevented && has_non_directory_host;

    let mut jobs = Vec::new();
    for host in opts.hosts.iter() {
        if problematic && !host.path().ends_with('/') {
            continue;
        }
        scanned.insert(host.clone());
        if let Validation::Scan(validator) =
            validate_directory(&mut client, host, &opts, &output_tx)
        {
            let split = initial_split(host, &opts, &output_tx);
            jobs.push(ScanJob {
                host: host.clone(),
                folder: host.clone(),
                validator,
                split,
            });
        }
    }
    if problematic {
        loop {
            thread::park();
        }
    }
    let _ = initial_sender.send(jobs);

    let (initial_jobs, done_sender) = loop {
        match receiver.recv() {
            Ok(ScanMessage::Start(jobs, done_sender)) => break (jobs, done_sender),
            Ok(_) => continue,
            Err(_) => return,
        }
    };

    for job in &initial_jobs {
        scanned.insert(job.folder.clone());
    }

    let mut active_workers = 0usize;
    for job in initial_jobs {
        dispatch_job(
            job,
            &opts,
            &output_tx,
            &scan_tx,
            &mut active_workers,
            &mut scanned,
        );
    }

    if active_workers == 0 {
        let _ = done_sender.send(());
        return;
    }

    while let Ok(message) = receiver.recv() {
        match message {
            ScanMessage::QueueDirectory(host, folder) => {
                if scanned.contains(&folder) {
                    continue;
                }
                scanned.insert(folder.clone());
                if let Validation::Scan(validator) =
                    validate_directory(&mut client, &folder, &opts, &output_tx)
                {
                    dispatch_job(
                        ScanJob {
                            host,
                            folder,
                            validator,
                            split: opts.wordlist_split,
                        },
                        &opts,
                        &output_tx,
                        &scan_tx,
                        &mut active_workers,
                        &mut scanned,
                    );
                }
            }
            ScanMessage::WorkerFinished => {
                active_workers -= 1;
                if active_workers == 0 {
                    break;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    let _ = done_sender.send(());
}

        for f in files:
            saved[f]=normalize(open(f).read(),srv.base) if os.path.exists(f) else None

        oo=(o[0],"\n".join(sorted(o[1].splitlines())),o[2],o[3],o[4]);nn=(n[0],"\n".join(sorted(n[1].splitlines())),n[2],n[3],n[4])
    if oo!=nn:
        print("DIFF",label)
        labels=["code","stdout","stderr","requests","files"]
        for i,lab in enumerate(labels):
            if oo[i]!=nn[i]: print(f" {lab} orig={oo[i]!r}\n {lab} new={nn[i]!r}")
        return False
    else:

src/request_thread.rs:153:/// Directory responses deliberately bypass these checks: they have
/// is followed manually, exactly once, so that the second
/// response can be classified as a (possibly listable) directory.
///
pub fn request(
    client: &mut CurlClient,
    url: &Url,
    is_directory: bool,
    opts: &GlobalOpts,
) -> ContentItem {
    // The URL recorded in a ContentItem, and used in error and trace
    // messages, is the URL constructed from the scan folder and the
    // wordlist entry. Credentials supplied on the command line are
    // added only to the copy handed to curl, a few lines below in
    // `perform_request`; they are not baked into reported results.
    log::trace!("Requesting {}", url);
    let raw_curl_response = match client.perform_request(url, is_directory, opts) {
        Ok(raw) => raw,
        Err(error) => {
            println!("Curl error after requesting {} : {}", url, error);
            return ContentItem::new(url.clone(), is_directory);
        }
    };

    // Keep the byte count from before the lossy text conversion;
    // it is the response size reported to the user even when the
    // response is binary. The text itself is only retained (in
    // lower case) so that directory listings can be recognised
    // and, when requested, scraped. It is not serialised into
    // any of the report formats. The body itself is not
    // retained once this function returns.
    //
    let size = raw_curl_response.body.len();
    let contents = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw_curl_response.body).into_owned().to_lowercase();
    let is_listable = is_directory && raw_curl_response.code == 200
        && (contents.contains("directory listing for")
            || contents.contains("parent directory")
            || contents.contains("up to higher"));

    let mut item = ContentItem {
        url: url.clone(),
        code: raw_curl_response.code,
        size,
        is_directory,
        is_listable,
        redirect_url: String::new(),
        found_from_listable: false,
        contents,
    };

    if item.code == 301 || item.code == 302 {
        // libcurl reports the redirect target in percent-encoded
        // form. The reported destination, and the destination
        // used when deciding whether this response points at the
        // slash-terminated form of the requested URL, is the
        // percent-decoded form. That distinction is observable
        // for targets containing (for example) encoded spaces,
        // question marks or non-ASCII text, so it is important
        // not to "tidy" the value by parsing it as a URL and
        // serialising it again here. The two unwraps below are
        // also observable for redirects with no Location header
        // and for percent-encoded bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
        let redirect = raw_curl_response.redirect_url.unwrap();
        let decoded_bytes = percent_decode_bytes(&redirect);
        item.redirect_url = std::str::from_utf8(&decoded_bytes).unwrap().to_owned();
    }

    if !is_directory
        && (item.code == 301 || item.code == 302)
        && item.redirect_url == format!("{}/", url)
    {
        let directory_url = Url::parse(&item.redirect_url).unwrap();
        return request(client, &directory_url, true, opts);
    }
    item
}

pub fn url_for_word(base: &url::Url, w: &str) -> url::Url {
    // Wordlist entries are deliberately not restricted to
    // simple path segments. Joining with the WHATWG rules
    // gives entries such as absolute URLs, protocol-relative
    // URLs, dot segments, queries and fragments the meanings
    // that the scanner has historically given them.
    //
    // An entry that cannot be parsed even with a base URL is
    // a programming or input error that the original scanner
    // exposed as a panic, so preserve that behaviour here.
    // The caller is responsible for cleaning the word first.
    base.join(w).unwrap()
}

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x /usr/local/cargo/bin/cargo ]; then
    PATH="/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH"
    export PATH
fi
if [ -z "${CARGO_HOME:-}" ] && [ -d /usr/local/cargo ]; then
    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo
    export CARGO_HOME
fi
if [ -z "${RUSTUP_HOME:-}" ] && [ -d /usr/local/rustup ]; then
    RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup
    export RUSTUP_HOME
fi

# The program links to the system libcurl. Install its development
# package on Debian-like systems if the linker cannot find it.
if ! ld -lcurl -o /dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        apt-get update && apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev || true
    fi
fi

if ! cargo build --release --offline; then
    cargo build --release
fi
rm -f ./executable
cp target/release/dirble ./executable
